import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Serre's conjecture II

Serre's conjecture II states that if $G$ is a simply connected semisimple algebraic group over a
perfect field $F$ of cohomological dimension at most $2$, then the Galois cohomology set
$H^1(F, G)$ is zero.

Algebraic groups over $F$ are modelled as group objects in the category of schemes over
$\operatorname{Spec} F$. A *linear algebraic group* is a smooth affine group scheme of finite type.
Such a group $G$ is *semisimple* if it is connected and the radical of $G_{\bar F}$ is trivial,
i.e. $G_{\bar F}$ has no nontrivial smooth connected commutative normal subgroup. It is
*simply connected* if every central isogeny $G' \to G$ from a connected linear algebraic group
$G'$ is an isomorphism.

Let $F_s$ be a separable closure of $F$ and $\Gamma_F = \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ its absolute
Galois group, a profinite group. The field $F$ has *cohomological dimension* at most $n$ if
$H^q(\Gamma_F, A) = 0$ for every discrete torsion $\Gamma_F$-module $A$ and every $q > n$. The
Galois cohomology set $H^1(F, G) = H^1(\Gamma_F, G(F_s))$ is the pointed set of continuous
$1$-cocycles $\Gamma_F \to G(F_s)$ modulo the relation of being cohomologous; it is zero if every
continuous $1$-cocycle is a coboundary. For a perfect field $F$ one has $F_s = \bar F$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Serre's conjecture II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serre%27s_conjecture_II_%28algebra%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- J.-P. Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne des groupes algébriques linéaires*, Colloque sur la
  théorie des groupes algébriques, Bruxelles (1962).
- J.-P. Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne*, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 5, Springer (1994),
  Chapter I §3, Chapter II §2 and Chapter III §3.1.
-/
namespace SerresConjectureII
open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Limits
open scoped MonObj GrpObj
universe u
/- ### Cohomological dimension of a field -/

blocks.code:
def CohomologicalDimensionLE (F : Type u) [Field F] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Action (TopModuleCat.{u} ℤ) Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)),
    DiscreteTopology A.V → AddMonoid.IsTorsion A.V →
    Continuous (fun p : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) × A.V ↦ (A.ρ p.1).hom p.2) →
    ∀ q, n < q → Subsingleton ((continuousCohomology ℤ Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) q).obj A)
blocks.docstring:
The field $F$ has cohomological dimension at most $n$: for every discrete torsion
$\Gamma_F$-module $A$ (a torsion abelian group with the discrete topology on which the absolute
Galois group $\Gamma_F = \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$, with its Krull topology, acts continuously)
and every $q > n$, the continuous cohomology group $H^q(\Gamma_F, A)$ vanishes.
See Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne*, Chapter I §3.1 and Chapter II §2.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `continuousCohomology` (Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ContinuousCohomology.Basic) is used as the cohomology theory; `groupCohomology` was rejected because it ignores the profinite topology; `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup` was not used because it is a `def` (no `IsTopologicalGroup` instance) and is built from the algebraic closure, while Serre's definitions use the separable closure (the two coincide for perfect fields).
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.CohomologicalDimensionLE
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of the (p-)cohomological dimension of a profinite group or of a field. Defined literally following Serre (Cohomologie galoisienne I §3.1, II §2): cd(F) ≤ n iff for every discrete torsion Gal(F_s/F)-module A (discrete topology, torsion, continuous action) and every q > n the continuous cohomology H^q vanishes. Equivalent to sup_p cd_p ≤ n since H^q(Γ, A) is torsion for torsion A.

blocks.name: CohomologicalDimensionLE
blocks.text:
/-- The field $F$ has cohomological dimension at most $n$: for every discrete torsion
$\Gamma_F$-module $A$ (a torsion abelian group with the discrete topology on which the absolute
Galois group $\Gamma_F = \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$, with its Krull topology, acts continuously)
and every $q > n$, the continuous cohomology group $H^q(\Gamma_F, A)$ vanishes.
See Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne*, Chapter I §3.1 and Chapter II §2. -/
def CohomologicalDimensionLE (F : Type u) [Field F] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Action (TopModuleCat.{u} ℤ) Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)),
    DiscreteTopology A.V → AddMonoid.IsTorsion A.V →
    Continuous (fun p : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) × A.V ↦ (A.ρ p.1).hom p.2) →
    ∀ q, n < q → Subsingleton ((continuousCohomology ℤ Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) q).obj A)
/- ### Algebraic groups -/
section AlgebraicGroups
variable {S : Scheme.{u}}

blocks.code:
class IsLinearAlgebraicGroup (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop where
  isAffineHom : IsAffineHom G.X.hom
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom
  isSmooth : IsSmooth G.X.hom
blocks.docstring:
A group scheme `G` over `S` is a *linear algebraic group* if its structure morphism is
affine, of finite type and smooth.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Grp (Over S)` with `Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory` (used as the underlying group scheme notion); `HopfAlgebra` (rejected: no points functor/group structure or subgroup theory available).
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.IsLinearAlgebraicGroup
justification.why_needed: No notion of (linear) algebraic group in Mathlib. A group object in `Over S` whose structure morphism is affine, locally of finite type and smooth (Serre's algebraic groups are smooth varieties).

blocks.name: IsLinearAlgebraicGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A group scheme `G` over `S` is a *linear algebraic group* if its structure morphism is
affine, of finite type and smooth. -/
class IsLinearAlgebraicGroup (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop where
  isAffineHom : IsAffineHom G.X.hom
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom
  isSmooth : IsSmooth G.X.hom

blocks.code:
structure IsNormalSubgroupScheme {G H : Grp (Over S)} (f : H ⟶ G) : Prop where
  isClosedImmersion : IsClosedImmersion f.hom.hom.left
  conj_mem : ∀ (T : Over S) (g : T ⟶ G.X) (h : T ⟶ H.X),
    ∃ h' : T ⟶ H.X, (h' ≫ f.hom.hom) = g * (h ≫ f.hom.hom) * g⁻¹
blocks.docstring:
A homomorphism of group schemes `f : H ⟶ G` over `S` realises `H` as a *normal closed
subgroup scheme* of `G`: `f` is a closed immersion and, for every `S`-scheme `T`, the subgroup
`H(T)` of `G(T)` is normal.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Subgroup.Normal` (only for abstract groups); nothing for group schemes.
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.IsNormalSubgroupScheme
justification.why_needed: Needed to express the radical. A homomorphism of group objects that is a closed immersion and such that H(T) is normal in G(T) for all S-schemes T (functor-of-points normality, expressed with the Yoneda group structure `GrpObj.Hom.group`).

blocks.name: IsNormalSubgroupScheme
blocks.text:
/-- A homomorphism of group schemes `f : H ⟶ G` over `S` realises `H` as a *normal closed
subgroup scheme* of `G`: `f` is a closed immersion and, for every `S`-scheme `T`, the subgroup
`H(T)` of `G(T)` is normal. -/
structure IsNormalSubgroupScheme {G H : Grp (Over S)} (f : H ⟶ G) : Prop where
  isClosedImmersion : IsClosedImmersion f.hom.hom.left
  conj_mem : ∀ (T : Over S) (g : T ⟶ G.X) (h : T ⟶ H.X),
    ∃ h' : T ⟶ H.X, (h' ≫ f.hom.hom) = g * (h ≫ f.hom.hom) * g⁻¹

blocks.docstring:
A group scheme `G` over `S` has *trivial radical* if every smooth connected commutative
normal closed subgroup scheme of `G` is trivial, i.e. its structure morphism is an isomorphism.
Over an algebraically closed field this says that the radical of `G` (the largest smooth
connected solvable normal subgroup) is trivial: the last nontrivial term of the derived series of
the radical is a smooth connected commutative normal subgroup.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib (no `LieAlgebra`-based approach possible since F may have positive characteristic).
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.HasTrivialRadical
justification.why_needed: Semisimplicity requires the radical of G_{F̄} to be trivial. Encoded as: every smooth connected commutative normal closed subgroup scheme is trivial (structure morphism an iso). This is equivalent to triviality of the radical (largest smooth connected solvable normal subgroup) because the last nontrivial term of the derived series of the radical is a smooth connected commutative normal subgroup; this avoids formalising solvability/derived series of group schemes.

blocks.name: HasTrivialRadical
blocks.text:
/-- A group scheme `G` over `S` has *trivial radical* if every smooth connected commutative
normal closed subgroup scheme of `G` is trivial, i.e. its structure morphism is an isomorphism.
Over an algebraically closed field this says that the radical of `G` (the largest smooth
connected solvable normal subgroup) is trivial: the last nontrivial term of the derived series of
the radical is a smooth connected commutative normal subgroup. -/
def HasTrivialRadical (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Grp (Over S)) (f : H ⟶ G), IsNormalSubgroupScheme f →
    IsSmooth H.X.hom → ConnectedSpace H.X.left → IsCommMonObj H.X → IsIso H.X.hom

blocks.code:
structure IsCentralIsogeny {G' G : Grp (Over S)} (f : G' ⟶ G) : Prop where
  surjective : Surjective f.hom.hom.left
  isFinite_kernel : IsFinite (pullback.snd f.hom.hom.left η[G.X].left)
  central : ∀ (T : Over S) (g k : T ⟶ G'.X), (k ≫ f.hom.hom) = 1 → g * k = k * g
blocks.docstring:
A homomorphism of group schemes `f : G' ⟶ G` over `S` is a *central isogeny* if it is
surjective, its kernel `G' ×_G S` (the fibre of `f` over the unit section of `G`) is finite over
`S`, and its kernel is central in `G'`: for every `S`-scheme `T`, every element of `G'(T)`
commutes with every element of the kernel of `G'(T) → G(T)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No isogeny notion in Mathlib for group schemes.
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.IsCentralIsogeny
justification.why_needed: Simple connectedness is defined via central isogenies. A homomorphism f : G' ⟶ G that is surjective (as a morphism of schemes), whose kernel (pullback of f along the unit section) is finite over S, and whose kernel is central (for all T, elements of G'(T) killed by f commute with all of G'(T)).

blocks.name: IsCentralIsogeny
blocks.text:
/-- A homomorphism of group schemes `f : G' ⟶ G` over `S` is a *central isogeny* if it is
surjective, its kernel `G' ×_G S` (the fibre of `f` over the unit section of `G`) is finite over
`S`, and its kernel is central in `G'`: for every `S`-scheme `T`, every element of `G'(T)`
commutes with every element of the kernel of `G'(T) → G(T)`. -/
structure IsCentralIsogeny {G' G : Grp (Over S)} (f : G' ⟶ G) : Prop where
  surjective : Surjective f.hom.hom.left
  isFinite_kernel : IsFinite (pullback.snd f.hom.hom.left η[G.X].left)
  central : ∀ (T : Over S) (g k : T ⟶ G'.X), (k ≫ f.hom.hom) = 1 → g * k = k * g

blocks.code:
class IsSimplyConnected (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop where
  isIso_of_isCentralIsogeny : ∀ (G' : Grp (Over S)) (f : G' ⟶ G), IsLinearAlgebraicGroup G' →
    ConnectedSpace G'.X.left → IsCentralIsogeny f → IsIso f
blocks.docstring:
A group scheme `G` over `S` is *simply connected* if every central isogeny `G' ⟶ G` from a
connected linear algebraic group `G'` is an isomorphism.

justification.name: SerresConjectureII.IsSimplyConnected
justification.why_needed: A group scheme G is simply connected if every central isogeny G' ⟶ G from a connected linear algebraic group (smooth: this excludes e.g. G × α_p → G in characteristic p) is an isomorphism (Borel–Tits/Conrad definition; in characteristic p non-central isogenies such as Frobenius must be excluded).

blocks.name: IsSimplyConnected
blocks.text:
/-- A group scheme `G` over `S` is *simply connected* if every central isogeny `G' ⟶ G` from a
connected linear algebraic group `G'` is an isomorphism. -/
class IsSimplyConnected (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop where
  isIso_of_isCentralIsogeny : ∀ (G' : Grp (Over S)) (f : G' ⟶ G), IsLinearAlgebraicGroup G' →
    ConnectedSpace G'.X.left → IsCentralIsogeny f → IsIso f
variable (F : Type u) [Field F]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraicClosure (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) :
    Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (AlgebraicClosure F)))) :=
  (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F (AlgebraicClosure F))))).mapGrp.obj G
blocks.docstring:
The base change $G_{\bar F}$ of a group scheme `G` over a field `F` to an algebraic closure
$\bar F$ of `F`.

justification.name: SerresConjectureII.baseChangeAlgebraicClosure
justification.why_needed: The base change G_{F̄} via `(Over.pullback (Spec.map (algebraMap F F̄))).mapGrp`, used to state trivial radical over the algebraic closure.

blocks.name: baseChangeAlgebraicClosure
blocks.text:
/-- The base change $G_{\bar F}$ of a group scheme `G` over a field `F` to an algebraic closure
$\bar F$ of `F`. -/
noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraicClosure (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) :
    Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (AlgebraicClosure F)))) :=
  (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F (AlgebraicClosure F))))).mapGrp.obj G

blocks.code:
class IsSemisimple (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Prop where
  isLinearAlgebraicGroup : IsLinearAlgebraicGroup G
  connectedSpace : ConnectedSpace G.X.left
  hasTrivialRadical : HasTrivialRadical (baseChangeAlgebraicClosure F G)
blocks.docstring:
A group scheme `G` over a field `F` is a *semisimple algebraic group* if it is a connected
linear algebraic group (smooth, affine, of finite type) and the radical of $G_{\bar F}$ is
trivial.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `LieAlgebra.IsSemisimple` (only correct in characteristic 0; F may have positive characteristic).
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.IsSemisimple
justification.why_needed: Semisimple algebraic group over a field F: connected linear algebraic group whose base change to F̄ has trivial radical.

blocks.name: IsSemisimple
blocks.text:
variable {F} in
/-- A group scheme `G` over a field `F` is a *semisimple algebraic group* if it is a connected
linear algebraic group (smooth, affine, of finite type) and the radical of $G_{\bar F}$ is
trivial. -/
class IsSemisimple (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Prop where
  isLinearAlgebraicGroup : IsLinearAlgebraicGroup G
  connectedSpace : ConnectedSpace G.X.left
  hasTrivialRadical : HasTrivialRadical (baseChangeAlgebraicClosure F G)
end AlgebraicGroups
/- ### Galois cohomology -/
section GaloisCohomology
variable (F : Type u) [Field F]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def specSeparableClosure : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)) :=
  Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F (SeparableClosure F))))
blocks.docstring:
$\operatorname{Spec} F_s$ as a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec} F$, where $F_s$ is a separable
closure of $F$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `GrpObj.Hom.group` supplies the group structure; no existing Galois action on scheme points.
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.specSeparableClosure / specGal / Points
justification.why_needed: G(F_s) = Hom_{Spec F}(Spec F_s, G) with its Yoneda group structure, and the automorphism Spec(σ) of Spec F_s over Spec F for σ ∈ Gal(F_s/F).

blocks.name: specSeparableClosure
blocks.text:
/-- $\operatorname{Spec} F_s$ as a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec} F$, where $F_s$ is a separable
closure of $F$. -/
noncomputable def specSeparableClosure : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)) :=
  Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F (SeparableClosure F))))

blocks.code:
noncomputable def specGal (σ : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)) :
    specSeparableClosure F ⟶ specSeparableClosure F :=
  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (σ : SeparableClosure F →+* SeparableClosure F))) <| by
    simp only [specSeparableClosure, Over.mk_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    congr 2
    ext x
    simp
blocks.docstring:
The automorphism of $\operatorname{Spec} F_s$ over $\operatorname{Spec} F$ induced by
$\sigma \in \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `GrpObj.Hom.group` supplies the group structure; no existing Galois action on scheme points.
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.specSeparableClosure / specGal / Points
justification.why_needed: G(F_s) = Hom_{Spec F}(Spec F_s, G) with its Yoneda group structure, and the automorphism Spec(σ) of Spec F_s over Spec F for σ ∈ Gal(F_s/F).

blocks.name: specGal
blocks.text:
/-- The automorphism of $\operatorname{Spec} F_s$ over $\operatorname{Spec} F$ induced by
$\sigma \in \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$. -/
noncomputable def specGal (σ : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)) :
    specSeparableClosure F ⟶ specSeparableClosure F :=
  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (σ : SeparableClosure F →+* SeparableClosure F))) <| by
    simp only [specSeparableClosure, Over.mk_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    congr 2
    ext x
    simp

blocks.code:
abbrev Points (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Type u :=
  specSeparableClosure F ⟶ G.X
blocks.docstring: The group $G(F_s)$ of $F_s$-points of a group scheme `G` over `F`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `GrpObj.Hom.group` supplies the group structure; no existing Galois action on scheme points.
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.specSeparableClosure / specGal / Points
justification.why_needed: G(F_s) = Hom_{Spec F}(Spec F_s, G) with its Yoneda group structure, and the automorphism Spec(σ) of Spec F_s over Spec F for σ ∈ Gal(F_s/F).

blocks.name: Points
blocks.text:
/-- The group $G(F_s)$ of $F_s$-points of a group scheme `G` over `F`. -/
abbrev Points (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Type u :=
  specSeparableClosure F ⟶ G.X
variable {F}

blocks.code:
noncomputable instance (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) :
    MulDistribMulAction Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) (Points F G) where
  smul σ x := specGal F σ ≫ x
  one_smul x := by
    change (specGal F 1 ≫ x) = x
    have : specGal F 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
      have h : ((1 : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)) : SeparableClosure F →+* SeparableClosure F) =
          RingHom.id _ := by
        ext
        rfl
      simp [specGal, h]
      rfl
    rw [this, Category.id_comp]
  mul_smul σ τ x := by
    change (specGal F (σ * τ) ≫ x) = (specGal F σ ≫ (specGal F τ ≫ x))
    have : specGal F (σ * τ) = specGal F σ ≫ specGal F τ := by
      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
      simp only [specGal, Over.homMk_left, Over.comp_left, ← Spec.map_comp,
        ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
      rfl
    rw [this, Category.assoc]
  smul_mul σ x y := by
    change (specGal F σ ≫ (x * y)) = (specGal F σ ≫ x) * (specGal F σ ≫ y)
    rw [Hom.mul_def, Hom.mul_def, comp_lift_assoc]
  smul_one σ := by
    change (specGal F σ ≫ (1 : Points F G)) = 1
    rw [Hom.one_def, comp_toUnit_assoc]
blocks.docstring:
The natural action of $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ on the group $G(F_s)$ by group
automorphisms: $\sigma \in \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ acts on an $F_s$-point
$x \colon \operatorname{Spec} F_s \to G$ by precomposition with
$\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$.
blocks.text:
/-- The natural action of $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ on the group $G(F_s)$ by group
automorphisms: $\sigma \in \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ acts on an $F_s$-point
$x \colon \operatorname{Spec} F_s \to G$ by precomposition with
$\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$. -/
noncomputable instance (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) :
    MulDistribMulAction Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) (Points F G) where
  smul σ x := specGal F σ ≫ x
  one_smul x := by
    change (specGal F 1 ≫ x) = x
    have : specGal F 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
      have h : ((1 : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)) : SeparableClosure F →+* SeparableClosure F) =
          RingHom.id _ := by
        ext
        rfl
      simp [specGal, h]
      rfl
    rw [this, Category.id_comp]
  mul_smul σ τ x := by
    change (specGal F (σ * τ) ≫ x) = (specGal F σ ≫ (specGal F τ ≫ x))
    have : specGal F (σ * τ) = specGal F σ ≫ specGal F τ := by
      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
      simp only [specGal, Over.homMk_left, Over.comp_left, ← Spec.map_comp,
        ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
      rfl
    rw [this, Category.assoc]
  smul_mul σ x y := by
    change (specGal F σ ≫ (x * y)) = (specGal F σ ≫ x) * (specGal F σ ≫ y)
    rw [Hom.mul_def, Hom.mul_def, comp_lift_assoc]
  smul_one σ := by
    change (specGal F σ ≫ (1 : Points F G)) = 1
    rw [Hom.one_def, comp_toUnit_assoc]

blocks.code:
structure IsCocycle {G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))}
    (a : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) → Points F G) : Prop where
  isLocallyConstant : IsLocallyConstant a
  cocycle : ∀ σ τ, a (σ * τ) = a σ * σ • a τ
blocks.docstring:
A *continuous $1$-cocycle* of $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ with values in $G(F_s)$: a locally
constant map $a$ (i.e. a map continuous for the Krull topology on $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ and
the discrete topology on $G(F_s)$) with $a_{\sigma\tau} = a_\sigma \cdot \sigma(a_\tau)$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `groupCohomology.H1`/`oneCocycles` only handle abelian coefficients and ignore continuity.
justification.name: SerresConjectureII.IsCocycle
justification.why_needed: Continuous 1-cocycles Gal(F_s/F) → G(F_s): locally constant (= continuous for the Krull topology and discrete topology on G(F_s)) with a(στ) = a(σ)·σ(a(τ)) (Serre I §5.1).

blocks.name: IsCocycle
blocks.text:
/-- A *continuous $1$-cocycle* of $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ with values in $G(F_s)$: a locally
constant map $a$ (i.e. a map continuous for the Krull topology on $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ and
the discrete topology on $G(F_s)$) with $a_{\sigma\tau} = a_\sigma \cdot \sigma(a_\tau)$. -/
structure IsCocycle {G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))}
    (a : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) → Points F G) : Prop where
  isLocallyConstant : IsLocallyConstant a
  cocycle : ∀ σ τ, a (σ * τ) = a σ * σ • a τ

blocks.docstring:
The Galois cohomology set $H^1(F, G) = H^1(\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F), G(F_s))$ is zero:
every continuous $1$-cocycle is a coboundary, i.e. of the form
$\sigma \mapsto b^{-1} \cdot \sigma(b)$ for some $b \in G(F_s)$.

justification.name: SerresConjectureII.H1IsTrivial
justification.why_needed: H^1(F, G) = H^1(Gal(F_s/F), G(F_s)) is the trivial pointed set: every continuous 1-cocycle is a coboundary σ ↦ b⁻¹·σ(b).

blocks.name: H1IsTrivial
blocks.text:
/-- The Galois cohomology set $H^1(F, G) = H^1(\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F), G(F_s))$ is zero:
every continuous $1$-cocycle is a coboundary, i.e. of the form
$\sigma \mapsto b^{-1} \cdot \sigma(b)$ for some $b \in G(F_s)$. -/
def H1IsTrivial (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) → Points F G, IsCocycle a →
    ∃ b : Points F G, ∀ σ, a σ = b⁻¹ * σ • b
end GaloisCohomology

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop (∀ perfect field F with cd(F) ≤ 2, ∀ simply connected semisimple linear algebraic F-group G, H^1(F,G) = {*}): the unnamed 'perfect field' is implicitly F; 'zero' means the trivial pointed set for non-abelian Galois cohomology (every G-torsor over F has an F-point); cohomological dimension is the sup over primes ℓ of the ℓ-cohomological dimension of Gal(F̄/F); the article's converse, the imperfect-field/degree-of-imperfection ≤ 1 generalization (Serre 1994, arXiv:2308.00903, arXiv:2603.08061) and the many proved special cases are not posed by the statement and are omitted; despite the article's sentence 'proven for all groups over all perfect fields', the anisotropic E8 case over perfect fields remains open, so the category is research open.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 is the only candidate that produced a file, and its bespoke definitions check out against the literature on every point I verified. (1) cd(F) ≤ 2: for every discrete torsion Gal(F_s/F)-module (discrete topology + joint continuity = open stabilizers, i.e. Serre's discrete modules) and every q > 2, Mathlib's `continuousCohomology ℤ Γ q` vanishes; I checked that this is homology of G-invariant homogeneous continuous cochains C(Γ,C(Γ,…,A)) with ordinary ker/im homology in TopModuleCat (no closure), so for profinite Γ and discrete A it is Serre's H^q. Universe restriction on A is harmless since cd is detected by finite modules. (2) Semisimple: smooth affine finite-type connected group object in Over (Spec F) whose base change to F̄ has no nontrivial smooth connected commutative normal closed subgroup — equivalent to trivial radical (last nontrivial term of the derived series of R(G) is such a subgroup; conversely any such subgroup lies in R(G)); functorial normality equals point-normality for smooth groups over F̄. (3) Simply connected: every central isogeny (topologically surjective — equivalent to faithfully flat onto smooth G — with finite scheme-theoretic kernel G'×_G S and functorially central kernel) from a connected smooth affine group is an iso; smoothness of G' correctly excludes G×α_p→G in char p, and the root-datum argument gives equivalence with the standard definition in both directions, also over non-closed F since the universal cover is defined over F. (4) H^1(F,G)=1: locally constant (Krull topology, verified instance) cocycles Γ→G(F_s)=Hom_F(Spec F_s, G) with a(στ)=a(σ)·σ(a(τ)), all coboundaries b⁻¹σ(b); the Galois action σ•x = Spec(σ)≫x is the correct one (checked (σ*τ)x=σ(τx) and Spec.map_comp contravariance; mul_smul compiles). Main theorem: ∀ perfect F with cd ≤ 2, ∀ semisimple simply connected G, H1IsTrivial G — matches the statement. context:
In mathematics, specifically number theory, Serre's conjecture II is the statement that if G is a simply connected, semisimple algebraic group over a perfect field F of cohomological dimension at most 2, then the Galois cohomology set H1(F, G) is zero. It was proposed by Jean-Pierre Serre in 1962, as an higher-dimension equivalent of his conjecture I (which was later proven). 
A converse of the conjecture holds: if the field F is perfect and if the cohomology set H1(F, G) is zero for every semisimple, simply connected algebraic group G, then the p-cohomological dimension of F is at most 2 for every prime p. The conjecture has been proven for all groups over all perfect fields; however, it remains open for anisotropic E6, E7 and E8 groups and trialitarian D4 group over imperfect fields.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Serre's conjecture II

Serre's conjecture II states that if $G$ is a simply connected semisimple algebraic group over a
perfect field $F$ of cohomological dimension at most $2$, then the Galois cohomology set
$H^1(F, G)$ is zero.

Algebraic groups over $F$ are modelled as group objects in the category of schemes over
$\operatorname{Spec} F$. A *linear algebraic group* is a smooth affine group scheme of finite type.
Such a group $G$ is *semisimple* if it is connected and the radical of $G_{\bar F}$ is trivial,
i.e. $G_{\bar F}$ has no nontrivial smooth connected commutative normal subgroup. It is
*simply connected* if every central isogeny $G' \to G$ from a connected linear algebraic group
$G'$ is an isomorphism.

Let $F_s$ be a separable closure of $F$ and $\Gamma_F = \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ its absolute
Galois group, a profinite group. The field $F$ has *cohomological dimension* at most $n$ if
$H^q(\Gamma_F, A) = 0$ for every discrete torsion $\Gamma_F$-module $A$ and every $q > n$. The
Galois cohomology set $H^1(F, G) = H^1(\Gamma_F, G(F_s))$ is the pointed set of continuous
$1$-cocycles $\Gamma_F \to G(F_s)$ modulo the relation of being cohomologous; it is zero if every
continuous $1$-cocycle is a coboundary. For a perfect field $F$ one has $F_s = \bar F$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Serre's conjecture II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serre%27s_conjecture_II_%28algebra%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- J.-P. Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne des groupes algébriques linéaires*, Colloque sur la
  théorie des groupes algébriques, Bruxelles (1962).
- J.-P. Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne*, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 5, Springer (1994),
  Chapter I §3, Chapter II §2 and Chapter III §3.1.
-/

namespace SerresConjectureII

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Limits
open scoped MonObj GrpObj

universe u

/- ### Cohomological dimension of a field -/

/-- The field $F$ has cohomological dimension at most $n$: for every discrete torsion
$\Gamma_F$-module $A$ (a torsion abelian group with the discrete topology on which the absolute
Galois group $\Gamma_F = \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$, with its Krull topology, acts continuously)
and every $q > n$, the continuous cohomology group $H^q(\Gamma_F, A)$ vanishes.
See Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne*, Chapter I §3.1 and Chapter II §2. -/
def CohomologicalDimensionLE (F : Type u) [Field F] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Action (TopModuleCat.{u} ℤ) Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)),
    DiscreteTopology A.V → AddMonoid.IsTorsion A.V →
    Continuous (fun p : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) × A.V ↦ (A.ρ p.1).hom p.2) →
    ∀ q, n < q → Subsingleton ((continuousCohomology ℤ Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) q).obj A)

/- ### Algebraic groups -/

section AlgebraicGroups

variable {S : Scheme.{u}}

/-- A group scheme `G` over `S` is a *linear algebraic group* if its structure morphism is
affine, of finite type and smooth. -/
class IsLinearAlgebraicGroup (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop where
  isAffineHom : IsAffineHom G.X.hom
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom
  isSmooth : IsSmooth G.X.hom

/-- A homomorphism of group schemes `f : H ⟶ G` over `S` realises `H` as a *normal closed
subgroup scheme* of `G`: `f` is a closed immersion and, for every `S`-scheme `T`, the subgroup
`H(T)` of `G(T)` is normal. -/
structure IsNormalSubgroupScheme {G H : Grp (Over S)} (f : H ⟶ G) : Prop where
  isClosedImmersion : IsClosedImmersion f.hom.hom.left
  conj_mem : ∀ (T : Over S) (g : T ⟶ G.X) (h : T ⟶ H.X),
    ∃ h' : T ⟶ H.X, (h' ≫ f.hom.hom) = g * (h ≫ f.hom.hom) * g⁻¹

/-- A group scheme `G` over `S` has *trivial radical* if every smooth connected commutative
normal closed subgroup scheme of `G` is trivial, i.e. its structure morphism is an isomorphism.
Over an algebraically closed field this says that the radical of `G` (the largest smooth
connected solvable normal subgroup) is trivial: the last nontrivial term of the derived series of
the radical is a smooth connected commutative normal subgroup. -/
def HasTrivialRadical (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Grp (Over S)) (f : H ⟶ G), IsNormalSubgroupScheme f →
    IsSmooth H.X.hom → ConnectedSpace H.X.left → IsCommMonObj H.X → IsIso H.X.hom

/-- A homomorphism of group schemes `f : G' ⟶ G` over `S` is a *central isogeny* if it is
surjective, its kernel `G' ×_G S` (the fibre of `f` over the unit section of `G`) is finite over
`S`, and its kernel is central in `G'`: for every `S`-scheme `T`, every element of `G'(T)`
commutes with every element of the kernel of `G'(T) → G(T)`. -/
structure IsCentralIsogeny {G' G : Grp (Over S)} (f : G' ⟶ G) : Prop where
  surjective : Surjective f.hom.hom.left
  isFinite_kernel : IsFinite (pullback.snd f.hom.hom.left η[G.X].left)
  central : ∀ (T : Over S) (g k : T ⟶ G'.X), (k ≫ f.hom.hom) = 1 → g * k = k * g

/-- A group scheme `G` over `S` is *simply connected* if every central isogeny `G' ⟶ G` from a
connected linear algebraic group `G'` is an isomorphism. -/
class IsSimplyConnected (G : Grp (Over S)) : Prop where
  isIso_of_isCentralIsogeny : ∀ (G' : Grp (Over S)) (f : G' ⟶ G), IsLinearAlgebraicGroup G' →
    ConnectedSpace G'.X.left → IsCentralIsogeny f → IsIso f

variable (F : Type u) [Field F]

/-- The base change $G_{\bar F}$ of a group scheme `G` over a field `F` to an algebraic closure
$\bar F$ of `F`. -/
noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraicClosure (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) :
    Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (AlgebraicClosure F)))) :=
  (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F (AlgebraicClosure F))))).mapGrp.obj G

variable {F} in
/-- A group scheme `G` over a field `F` is a *semisimple algebraic group* if it is a connected
linear algebraic group (smooth, affine, of finite type) and the radical of $G_{\bar F}$ is
trivial. -/
class IsSemisimple (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Prop where
  isLinearAlgebraicGroup : IsLinearAlgebraicGroup G
  connectedSpace : ConnectedSpace G.X.left
  hasTrivialRadical : HasTrivialRadical (baseChangeAlgebraicClosure F G)

end AlgebraicGroups

/- ### Galois cohomology -/

section GaloisCohomology

variable (F : Type u) [Field F]

/-- $\operatorname{Spec} F_s$ as a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec} F$, where $F_s$ is a separable
closure of $F$. -/
noncomputable def specSeparableClosure : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)) :=
  Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F (SeparableClosure F))))

/-- The automorphism of $\operatorname{Spec} F_s$ over $\operatorname{Spec} F$ induced by
$\sigma \in \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$. -/
noncomputable def specGal (σ : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)) :
    specSeparableClosure F ⟶ specSeparableClosure F :=
  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (σ : SeparableClosure F →+* SeparableClosure F))) <| by
    simp only [specSeparableClosure, Over.mk_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    congr 2
    ext x
    simp

/-- The group $G(F_s)$ of $F_s$-points of a group scheme `G` over `F`. -/
abbrev Points (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Type u :=
  specSeparableClosure F ⟶ G.X

variable {F}

/-- The natural action of $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ on the group $G(F_s)$ by group
automorphisms: $\sigma \in \operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ acts on an $F_s$-point
$x \colon \operatorname{Spec} F_s \to G$ by precomposition with
$\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$. -/
noncomputable instance (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) :
    MulDistribMulAction Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) (Points F G) where
  smul σ x := specGal F σ ≫ x
  one_smul x := by
    change (specGal F 1 ≫ x) = x
    have : specGal F 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
      have h : ((1 : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F)) : SeparableClosure F →+* SeparableClosure F) =
          RingHom.id _ := by
        ext
        rfl
      simp [specGal, h]
      rfl
    rw [this, Category.id_comp]
  mul_smul σ τ x := by
    change (specGal F (σ * τ) ≫ x) = (specGal F σ ≫ (specGal F τ ≫ x))
    have : specGal F (σ * τ) = specGal F σ ≫ specGal F τ := by
      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
      simp only [specGal, Over.homMk_left, Over.comp_left, ← Spec.map_comp,
        ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
      rfl
    rw [this, Category.assoc]
  smul_mul σ x y := by
    change (specGal F σ ≫ (x * y)) = (specGal F σ ≫ x) * (specGal F σ ≫ y)
    rw [Hom.mul_def, Hom.mul_def, comp_lift_assoc]
  smul_one σ := by
    change (specGal F σ ≫ (1 : Points F G)) = 1
    rw [Hom.one_def, comp_toUnit_assoc]

/-- A *continuous $1$-cocycle* of $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ with values in $G(F_s)$: a locally
constant map $a$ (i.e. a map continuous for the Krull topology on $\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F)$ and
the discrete topology on $G(F_s)$) with $a_{\sigma\tau} = a_\sigma \cdot \sigma(a_\tau)$. -/
structure IsCocycle {G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))}
    (a : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) → Points F G) : Prop where
  isLocallyConstant : IsLocallyConstant a
  cocycle : ∀ σ τ, a (σ * τ) = a σ * σ • a τ

/-- The Galois cohomology set $H^1(F, G) = H^1(\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F), G(F_s))$ is zero:
every continuous $1$-cocycle is a coboundary, i.e. of the form
$\sigma \mapsto b^{-1} \cdot \sigma(b)$ for some $b \in G(F_s)$. -/
def H1IsTrivial (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) → Points F G, IsCocycle a →
    ∃ b : Points F G, ∀ σ, a σ = b⁻¹ * σ • b

end GaloisCohomology

/-- **Serre's conjecture II.** If $G$ is a simply connected semisimple algebraic group over a
perfect field $F$ of cohomological dimension at most $2$, then the Galois cohomology set
$H^1(F, G) = H^1(\operatorname{Gal}(\bar F/F), G(\bar F))$ is zero, i.e. every continuous
$1$-cocycle $\operatorname{Gal}(\bar F/F) \to G(\bar F)$ is a coboundary. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 14 20]
theorem serres_conjecture_ii (F : Type u) [Field F] [PerfectField F]
    (hF : CohomologicalDimensionLE F 2)
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) [IsSemisimple G] [IsSimplyConnected G] :
    H1IsTrivial G := by
  sorry

/-- The constant map $\sigma \mapsto 1$ is a continuous $1$-cocycle. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 12 14 20]
theorem isCocycle_one {F : Type u} [Field F] (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))) :
    IsCocycle (fun _ : Gal(SeparableClosure F/F) ↦ (1 : Points F G)) where
  isLocallyConstant := IsLocallyConstant.const 1
  cocycle σ τ := by simp

/-- The identity of a group scheme is a central isogeny. -/
@[category API, AMS 14 20]
theorem isCentralIsogeny_id {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Grp (Over S)) : IsCentralIsogeny (𝟙 G) where
  surjective := by
    change Surjective (𝟙 G.X.left)
    infer_instance
  isFinite_kernel := by
    change IsFinite (pullback.snd (𝟙 G.X.left) η[G.X].left)
    have : IsIso (pullback.snd (𝟙 G.X.left) η[G.X].left) := inferInstance
    exact MorphismProperty.of_isIso @IsFinite _
  central T g k hk := by
    change (k ≫ 𝟙 G.X) = 1 at hk
    rw [Category.comp_id] at hk
    rw [hk, one_mul, mul_one]

end SerresConjectureII

items: Algebraic groups over F are group objects `Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)))` with the cartesian monoidal structure `Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory` (local instance); all objects live in universe u with F : Type u.
"Algebraic group" is taken in Serre's sense (smooth): `IsLinearAlgebraicGroup` = affine + locally of finite type + smooth structure morphism.

Semisimple = connected linear algebraic group whose base change to `AlgebraicClosure F` has trivial radical; trivial radical is encoded as "no nontrivial smooth connected *commutative* normal closed subgroup scheme" instead of "solvable" (equivalent via the derived series of the radical). Normality is functor-of-points normality for all S-schemes T; "trivial" means the structure morphism is an isomorphism.

Simply connected = every central isogeny from a connected linear algebraic (hence smooth) group is an isomorphism; isogeny = surjective on underlying spaces with kernel (pullback of f along the unit section) finite over the base; central = kernel elements commute with all T-points. Smoothness of G' is essential in characteristic p (excludes G × α_p → G).

H^1(F, G) is formalised as Serre's Galois cohomology H^1(Gal(F_s/F), G(F_s)) via continuous (locally constant) 1-cocycles into G(F_s) = Hom_{Spec F}(Spec F_s, G) with the Yoneda group law, and the Galois action by precomposition with Spec(σ); 'zero' = every cocycle is a coboundary b⁻¹·σ(b). The separable closure `SeparableClosure F` is used (Serre's definition); for the perfect fields of the conjecture it equals the algebraic closure. The alternative reading in the decomposition notes (every G-torsor has an F-point) is equivalent for smooth G.

Cohomological dimension ≤ 2 is stated as: for every discrete torsion Gal(F_s/F)-module A (object of `Action (TopModuleCat.{u} ℤ) Γ` with discrete topology, torsion carrier and jointly continuous action) and every q > 2, Mathlib's `continuousCohomology ℤ Γ q` of A is a subsingleton. This is Serre's definition of cd(Γ) = sup_p cd_p(Γ) ≤ 2 (vanishing of all p-primary parts of the torsion group H^q(Γ, A)). Using all torsion modules rather than only finite ones, and all q > 2 rather than only q = 3, follows the literal definition.
The hypothesis `PerfectField F` is kept as in the statement even though the definitions are stated with the separable closure and are meaningful for all fields.
Two `@[category API]` sanity theorems are included: the constant cocycle 1 is a cocycle, and the identity is a central isogeny.

reviewer_notes: Seven of eight candidates (c01–c03, c05–c08) bailed out with missing_primitives, arguing that algebraic groups, semisimplicity, simple connectedness, non-abelian H^1 and cd of a field are absent from Mathlib. Those are real gaps, but c04 shows they can be bridged faithfully from existing Mathlib primitives: group objects `Grp (Over (Spec F))` with the cartesian structure (Yoneda group law on T-points), scheme morphism properties (IsAffineHom, LocallyOfFiniteType, IsSmooth, IsClosedImmersion, Surjective, IsFinite), `Over.pullback` base change, the Krull-topologised Gal(F_s/F), and `continuousCohomology`. The char-p pitfalls the bail-outs raised (SL_p→PGL_p bijective on points; infinitesimal kernels) are handled correctly by c04 via scheme-theoretic kernels, functorial centrality and the smoothness requirement on the source of central isogenies. Ambiguities in the original: the unnamed perfect field is F (as the table says); 'zero' = trivial pointed set, encoded as every continuous cocycle being a coboundary (equivalent to every G-torsor having an F-point for smooth G); H^1 and cd use the separable closure, which equals F̄ for perfect F. The residual risk is inherent to a ~150-line bespoke development of algebraic-group notions with no library API to test against; I verified each definition by hand (including the derived-series argument for HasTrivialRadical and the root-datum argument for IsSimplyConnected) and found no discrepancy. Two API theorems from c04 are retained. Status research open is correct (anisotropic E8 over perfect fields remains open).
statement: Serre's conjecture II: if $G$ is a simply connected semisimple algebraic group over a perfect field of cohomological dimension at most $2$, then the Galois cohomology set $H^{1}(F, G)$ is zero.
